delete_receipt.bounded_claim: In the source-backed ecommerce Phoenix/Ecto example, a previously searchable hard-deleted product is absent from raw tenant-scoped search hits after the explicit host delete and controlled persisted Oban work drain, while its sibling remains visible.
scenario_path: Seed the known product and drain prior indexing work.
Require the unique fixture name to appear in tenant-scoped search before deletion.
Call the explicit host deletion endpoint, which deletes the source row and invokes Scrypath deletion configured for persisted Oban work.
Drain the queued delete work, then poll the same endpoint's raw result.hits until the target name is absent.
Load the storefront and require the sibling product to remain visible while the target is absent.
limits: The claim is limited to the named ecommerce hard-delete Oban workflow and the exact historical source receipt.
The oracle uses a unique fixture name and raw result.hits after known presence; it has no separate source-row readback assertion and does not assert delete task UID correlation.

It does not prove package-backed deletion, inline/manual deletion, atomic source-delete/job-enqueue behavior, duplicate delivery idempotency, concurrency or recreation ordering, retries, restart recovery, production scheduling latency, soft deletes, arbitrary host policies, or all host applications.
